newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - Indian GDRs end down after Bombay fall.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - Indian GDRs end down after Bombay fall.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts fell in line with losses in Bombay earlier on Monday, amid political uncertainty and ahead of a local market holiday on Tuesday.
Traders said the market remained nervous and was unlikely to show much change until an April 11 confidence vote on the coalition government of Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda.
"There is a wait-and-see attitude ahead of April 11. Not much is going to happen before then," said a trader.
The key factor affecting sentiment was the likely future of the 1997/8 budget, which has not yet been passed by government.
Key prices were broadly lower, with Bajaj down 93 cents at $34.00/35.50, and Hindalco off 87 cents to $29/30.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index JCEAI closed 1.62 points, or 2.2 percent, down at 71.97 points, with the premium over the local market at 18.26 percent from 18.91 percent on Friday.
The Bombay Stock Exchange 30-share index shed 29.88 to 3,520.49.
The Capel Korea GDR Index ended 2.27 points, or 3.72 percent, up at 63.20, a premium of 27.12 percent over the local market.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index ended sharply higher after good gains in Taipei, adding up 9.08 points, or 7.29 percent, at 133.55, a discount of 2.73 percent.
